t: A Great Lakes kingdom ruled by the Nyiginya dynasty, whose sacred mwami governed through army, land and cattle chiefs.
It reached its greatest extent and centralisation under Kigeli IV Rwabugiri in the late nineteenth century.
German and Belgian rule hardened Hutu and Tutsi into fixed categories; the monarchy was abolished in 1961.
dyk: Rwanda had no fixed capital for most of its history: the royal court moved between residences, Nyanza became the permanent seat only around 1899, and Kigali began as a German residency in 1907.
ev: Ruganzu II Ndori establishes the Nyiginya kingdom in central Rwanda
Mutara II Rwogera annexes the Kingdom of Gisaka
Kigeli IV Rwabugiri dies on campaign after decades of expansion
The Coup of Rucunshu brings Yuhi V Musinga to the throne
Rwanda accepts German protection and joins German East Africa
Belgium deposes Musinga and installs Mutara III Rudahigwa
Mutara III dies and the Hutu revolution begins
A UN-supervised referendum confirms the abolition of the monarchy

f.capital: Shifting royal residences; Nyanza from c. 1899
